docuLanguageResource.title: Commission unconditionally approves UniCredit's acquisition of Commerzbank
docuLanguageResource.subtitle: Commission unconditionally approves UniCredit's acquisition of Commerzbank
docuLanguageResource.htmlContent:
The European Commission has unconditionally approved, under the EU Merger Regulation, the proposed acquisition by UniCredit of Commerzbank. The Commission concluded that the transaction would raise no competition concerns in the European Economic Area (‘EEA').

UniCredit is an Italian banking group, providing retail and corporate banking services across Europe, particularly in Italy, Germany, Central and Eastern Europe. Commerzbank is a German banking group active in both retail and corporate banking, mainly in Germany.

Cross-border consolidation of the EU banking sector can help overcome national economic fragmentation, unlock economies of scale, and strengthen the Single Market, thereby enhancing the competitiveness of EU banks and their capacity to finance the European economy.

author.authorName: Teresa Ribera, Executive Vice-President for Clean, Just and Competitive Transition

dolaQuoteResources.extract: Europe needs stronger banks that can compete, grow and support our businesses and families. Cross-border mergers can help make this happen, allowing banks to operate more efficiently and better withstand economic shocks. But growth must not come at the expense of customers. Our approval of UniCredit’s acquisition of Commerzbank shows that it is possible to support a stronger European banking sector while safeguarding competition and choice.
